transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-30
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Asteria ML Platform Lead), Tom Nguyen (Asteria Infra), Priya Shah (Asteria Data Scientist)
Shared artifacts: deck: https://redwood.example.com/decks/asteria-bench-v1.pdf, bench sheet: https://sheets.goo.gl/asteria-bench-xyz

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving time today, we wanted to walk through a sandbox bench and show how our Optimize console surfaces INT8 vs FP8 tradeoffs, and get your constraints.
[00:22] Lena (Asteria): Thanks Maya. Quick context — our latency SLO is 250ms p50 for short answers, but some flows can be longer. Cost is also a driver, right now inference spend is growing fast.
[00:35] Maya: Got it, we'll try to keep examples aligned to that. Ravi will demo live profiles in the sandbox and show quality diffs.
[00:44] Ravi (Redwood SE): Hi, hi. I'm going to share my screen — bear with me if the screenshare lags. We loaded three profiles: FP32 baseline, INT8 tuned profile, and an experimental FP8 profile.
[01:05] Tom (Asteria): Quick question before you start, is FP8 considered stable for rollout? Our security team wants predictable degradation.
[01:12] Ravi: Short answer: FP8 is new-ish, we treat it as a variant with tighter acceptance gating. We recommend canary rollouts with automatic fallback to INT8 or FP32 if quality metrics drift.
[01:28] Maya: And in the console we have auto-fallback policies — you can set SLA thresholds and if perplexity or eval score drops beyond X, it routes to the fallback variant.
[01:40] Priya (Asteria): How are you measuring quality in these runs? We need something reproducible — BLEU? ROUGE? or more task-specific metrics.
[01:50] Ravi: Good call — Optimize supports custom eval hooks. In this session we ran a holdout set of 250 prompts Asteria shared last week and measured token-level logprob delta and a heuristic answer-similarity score. We'll export both.
[02:06] [00:02:06] (background cross talk) Speaker 1: yeah yeah
[02:15] Maya: I'm going to show the console now — note the 'precision profile' card, it surfaces latency distribution, the quality delta heatmap, and the recommended batch sizes per profile.
[02:28] Ravi: For INT8 we applied a quantization-aware calibration using representative prompts; that reduces memory and increases throughput by ~2.1x on our gadget bench. FP8 gave a 2.6x throughput improvement on the same hardware but had higher variance on longer prompts.
[02:50] Lena: Can you give an example where FP8 fails? We're worried about hallucinations in medical descriptions.
[02:58] Ravi: Sure — on long multi-step diagnostic prompts we saw some factual drift in the FP8 runs, especially with prompt length > 512 tokens. On short Q/A (<= 128 tokens) FP8's fidelity was similar to INT8.
[03:15] Tom: That matches our concern — most PII redaction flows are short, but our summarization can be long.
[03:22] Priya: Did you try progressive precision — like keep KV cache in FP32 but quantize weights?
[03:30] Ravi: Yep, mixed-precision was one of the middle profiles. In the console it's called 'hybrid-keeper' — we keep attention KV in higher precision and quantize the matmul paths. It retained most quality while still giving ~1.7x speedup.
[03:48] Maya: Also note the 'prefix cache' recommendations — if you have repeated prompt prefixes (like system + instruction), caching those embeddings reduces the observed latency, which can help FP8 where compute gains are offset by variance.
[04:05] [00:04:05] Speaker 2 (auto-transcript): "kv cash" appears in notes — that's kv cache
[04:12] Priya: For our acceptance criteria we need both automated scores and a human spot-check. Can the console attach the golden responses next to model output?
[04:21] Ravi: Yes, Optimize allows aligned side-by-side diffs and you can tag outputs for manual review. We'll show the export in a second.
[04:32] Maya: Before we jump to raw results, quick qualification — what's your expected traffic distribution? Is this mostly low lat, single-request per user, or batch scoring?
[04:43] Lena: Mixed — real-time chat and batch report generation overnight. Realtime is priority for SLA.
[04:49] Ravi: That helps. For realtime we favor INT8 or hybrid; for offline batch FP8 is often fine to maximize cost savings.
[05:01] [00:05:01] (screen flicker)
[05:08] Ravi: OK, here's the bench sheet — columns: prompt_id, length, baseline_latency_ms, int8_latency_ms, fp8_latency_ms, quality_score_baseline, quality_score_int8, quality_score_fp8. You can see p50 and p95 split.
[05:30] Priya: I see p95 for FP8 spikes on certain IDs — do those correspond to long-context prompts?
[05:36] Ravi: Yes 103, 117, 142 are long-context summaries. We also logged GPU utilization — FP8 pushes higher utilization but sometimes causes tail latency spikes due to kernel scheduling variance.
[05:50] Tom: Could the runtime mitigate that with request shaping or smaller batch sizes?
[05:55] Ravi: Exactly — the console suggests smaller max batch size for FP8 and more aggressive per-tenant qos. There's also an ops knob: reserve a fraction of capacity for low-latency buckets so those requests don't wait behind big batches.
[06:10] Maya: I'll highlight the recommended policy card — it says: for mixed workloads set FP8 for batch routes, INT8 for realtime, enable fallback at delta-quality > 0.06, and reserve 10% capacity for realtime.
[06:24] Lena: That policy language is helpful, can we export that as JSON for our infra team?
[06:29] Maya: Yes, exportable policy JSON, plus a Terraform-friendly rollout plan template. We'll attach in the follow-up.
[06:39] [00:06:39] (Priya typing)
[06:45] Priya: On the quality delta metric — what's the scale? 0 to 1?
[06:49] Ravi: It's normalized similarity score where 1 is perfect match to golden. We report delta against baseline FP32, so negative numbers mean worse.
[06:58] Priya: For our clinical summaries we want delta >= 0.95. Is that realistic on INT8?
[07:05] Ravi: For short-form yes, many customers see >=0.97 on INT8 once calibrated. For summary tasks that are long, mixed precision or FP32 might be required.
[07:16] Tom: About calibration, how heavy is the calibration step? We don't want a manual, expensive process every time model or prompt distribution shifts.
[07:24] Ravi: The calibration is lightweight — we sample representative prompts and run one pass to gather activation ranges. It can be automated in CI and re-run on schedule or when a drift alert fires.
[07:36] Maya: We also integrate with your eval harness so you can schedule nightly calibration runs against a rolling sample.
[07:45] Lena: Security question: in private deployments can we keep all data on-prem and only use the control plane?
[07:52] Maya: Yes — Redwood Private supports a customer-managed control plane and VPC-only data plane. Keys remain in your KMS. We can provide SOC2/ISO artifacts; I'll attach the security pack.
[08:05] Tom: Are there any caveats for FP8 on certain GPU families?
[08:11] Ravi: FP8 kernel availability depends on vendor support; on Ampere some kernels are emulated and give less benefit. We provide a compatibility matrix in the console and will recommend hardware-suitable profiles.
[08:24] Priya: Could you show a concrete prompt example comparing outputs?
[08:29] Ravi: Sure — prompt 042 is a 90-token clinical note rewrite. Baseline FP32: (reads) "Patient shows no acute cardiopulmonary distress..." INT8: nearly identical, minor punctuation differences. FP8: inserted a sentence that slightly overstates timeline — that's the factual drift I mentioned.
[08:50] Maya: We'll paste the three outputs into the sheet for your review; you'll see diff highlights.
[08:56] [00:08:56] (small laughter)
[09:05] Lena: So for our rollout we likely need to keep FP8 as opt-in for batch jobs only and use INT8 for realtime, with a canary on 5% of users for a week. Does that align with recommendations?
[09:14] Maya: Yes that's a very standard pattern. Our suggested rollout plan in the playbook has exactly that: canary -> 5% -> 20% -> auto-increase with monitor windows.
[09:23] Ravi: And the console will auto-send regression alerts to Slack/email if quality or latency crosses thresholds.
[09:30] Priya: About costs — what kind of savings can we expect moving from FP32 to INT8 and FP8?
[09:37] Ravi: Rough numbers: INT8 ~40-55% cost reduction vs FP32 for inference CPU/GPU time depending on model shape; FP8 can hit 50-70% but with the caveats we discussed. We'll share a cost-model spreadsheet.
[09:50] Tom: Any hidden ops burden? Our infra team prefers less operational overhead.
[09:55] Maya: We find the console reduces ops work by automating profiling, generating rollout artifacts, and integrating with CI/CD. SEs like Ravi will help run first few benches. After that it's mostly self-serve.
[10:08] [00:10:08] (ambient office noise)
[10:16] Ravi: I'm going to walk through the sandbox steps you can run: 1) Upload sample prompts into the sandbox workspace; 2) choose baseline and two precision profiles; 3) run a sensitivity sweep which varies batch size and sequence length; 4) view heatmap and download CSV.
[10:36] Priya: Can we simulate mixed traffic — like 80% short realtime, 20% batch — in the sandbox?
[10:40] Ravi: Yes, there's a traffic-mixer option where you define routes and weights. It will compute weighted p50/p95 and give suggested route-level profiles.
[10:50] Lena: Great. One more: can we lock quant profiles to specific model versions during rollouts? We don't want a model update to auto-use an incompatible profile.
[10:59] Ravi: Absolutely — profiles are version-bound. The console prevents attaching a profile to a model if the compatibility check fails.
[11:07] [00:11:07] Speaker 3 (auto-caption): "rollout is blocked"
[11:10] Tom: For the canary, what telemetry will we get? Token-level cost, latency, error rates?
[11:15] Maya: Full telemetry: token breakdown, per-token latency, error rates, failover counts, and per-route cost. You can also hook your APM.
[11:27] Priya: Will the console preserve PII when we share outputs with Redwood engineers during bench runs?
[11:33] Ravi: You can scrub or pseudonymize before uploading. For private deployments, we don't access plaintext unless you opt into support access.
[11:42] Lena: Ok, seems aligned. Can you send the specific sandbox invite and a starter pipeline we can plug into our CI?
[11:49] Maya: Yes — next steps I'll send: sandbox invite, the playbook PDF, policy JSON export, and the bench spreadsheet.
[11:57] [00:11:57] (screen stops)
[12:02] Maya: Any other blockers?
[12:05] Priya: One small thing — how do we handle model drift detection for quant profiles? We want automatic rollbacks if quality suddenly drops.
[12:13] Ravi: The Optimize console supports drift detectors tied to eval sets; on drift you can auto-roll back to last known good profile and create an incident. We can customize thresholds.
[12:23] Tom: Would that trigger a support ticket or webhook?
[12:27] Maya: Both — you can have it open a ticket and call a webhook.
[12:31] Priya: Perfect.
[12:35] [00:12:35] (15 min of screen walkthrough omitted in transcript summary)
[27:40] Ravi: Coming back to the bench numbers — summary slide: INT8 satisfies realtime SLO for 92% of prompts with delta >= 0.97, FP8 reduces unit cost further but only meets delta >= 0.95 for 70% of prompts and misses tails.
[28:00] Lena: So operationally we treat FP8 as 'cost-tier' with strict QA gates.
[28:06] Maya: Correct. And we recommend tagging routes and only enabling FP8 for batch-only routes or for low-impact experiments.
[28:15] Priya: If we need to push a hotfix model update that affects quantization, does your rollout plan support emergency rollbacks?
[28:22] Ravi: Yes emergency rollback runs the last-good profile and can also pin traffic to FP32 while you triage.
[28:30] Tom: Any recommended observability thresholds to start with?
[28:33] Maya: Start with delta-quality threshold 0.05, p95 latency 2x your p50 target, and a 60-minute monitor window for canaries. We can tweak after first run.
[28:48] [00:28:48] (brief pause)
[28:56] Priya: Alright, timeline wise can we run the first bench next week?
[29:00] Maya: Yes, Ravi can run it with your sample prompts next Wednesday if that works.
[29:05] Lena: Works for us.
[29:08] Maya: I'll send calendar invite, and attach the playbook.
[29:13] [00:29:13] (closing remarks)
[29:20] Maya: Quick recap: Redwood will provide sandbox access, playbook, exportable policy JSON, and bench templates. Asteria will provide 500 prompts and acceptance criteria. Ravi will run the 3-variant bench and share CSVs. We'll reconvene after the bench to decide FP8 canary scope.
[29:40] Priya: Thanks, all.
[29:43] Lena: Thanks everyone.
[29:45] Tom: Thanks.
[29:47] Maya: I'll follow up via email with links and next steps.
[29:52] [00:29:52] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: some speaker attributions may be imperfect (auto-captions). Occasional mis-typed technical terms (e.g., "kv cash" for KV cache, "int eight" for INT8) reflect automated transcript artifacts.
